title: Session KV checksum drift leading to delayed GPU OOMs on long-lived sessions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers (hosted-to-dedicated migrations and on-prem private clusters) reported sporadic GPU OOMs after long-running multi-turn sessions (6+ hours). OOMs did not correlate with immediate load spikes; instead memory climbed slowly until node OOM. Initial heap metrics showed steady KV handle growth and growing slab fragmentation without proportional accounting in session metadata. Repro: long synthetic chat with repeated long prefixes and frequent partial-rollbacks increased per-session KV entries until OOM in ~4-12 hours depending on model and sequence length.
timeline_updates: 2026-03-10: Escalation opened after two dedicated customers reported repeated OOMs during nightly batch inference. Initial priority P0 assigned. Contacted customers for core dump artifacts and session traces.

2026-03-11: Reproduced on staging with stress harness using mixed-length turns and forced session handoff. Observed kv_handle_count increasing beyond expected retention window. Created memory profiler traces and heap snapshots.

2026-03-12: Identified checksum mismatch occurrences for session descriptors concurrent with async-evict operations. Began drafting hotpatch that adds an epoch guard on KV descriptor updates. Preparing PR for runtime hotfix.
2026-03-12: Notified impacted customers with temporary mitigations (evict heartbeat reduced to 60s, enforced session TTL of 2 hours for long-running workloads).
steps_taken: Collected customer heap profiles, core dumps, and SDK session payloads; attached PR logs to ticket and the incident channel.
Built deterministic reproducer using the session-fuzz harness that simulates partial prefix reuse / rollback patterns from customer traces.
Executed targeted experiments: toggling async-spill to synchronous path removed the leak, indicating a race in async path.
Applied rolling restart and temporary eviction-aggressiveness increase for affected dedicated pools as immediate mitigation.
Prepared and opened hotfix PRs (see linked_prs) and added unit/integration tests for session-evict races and KV descriptor reconciliation.
root_cause: A race between the async eviction/spill pipeline and the session descriptor update path permitted duplicate/ghost KV handles to be reinserted with stale size metadata. These ghost handles were not accounted correctly by the slab allocator because a checksum epoch mismatch bypassed the coalescing code path, leading to slow, unbounded perceived live allocations and severe slab fragmentation. Over multi-hour sessions this caused observed memory to climb and eventually triggered GPU OOMs in hosted, dedicated, and private deployments depending on workload shape.
fix_description: 1) Introduce an epoch-based guard on session KV descriptor updates so any async-evict/insert sees a matching epoch or is rejected and scheduled for reconciliation. 2) Add a lightweight reconciliation pass in the KV garbage collector that detects duplicate handles and coalesces them, correcting slab accounting. 3) Harden the async-spill path with an allocation_guard counter and temporary per-session write fencing during critical updates. 4) Add unit tests and a stress integration test (session-fuzz harness) that simulates partial-rollbacks and mixed TTL workloads.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge hotfix to runtime-1.23.0-hotfix branch, run full CI and extended mem-stress jobs. 2) Canary deploy to low-traffic dedicated cluster (canary-2) for 24 hours, monitor kv_handle_count, slab_fragmentation_ratio, and GPU memory headroom. 3) If stable, rollout to all dedicated zones over a 6-hour window with staggered restarts. 4) For hosted control plane apply a feature-flag patch to enable epoch-checks and run a gradual ramp; for private customers provide patch with upgrade notes. 5) Post-rollout, run reconciliation job across affected nodes to heal existing ghost handles.
customer_communication: 2026-03-10: Acknowledged escalation and requested core dumps and session traces. Suggested temporary TTL and eviction aggressiveness increase.
2026-03-11: Shared reproducer plan and ETA for hotfix (48-72h). Customer accepted temporary mitigations.
2026-03-12: Shared hotfix PR link and scheduled a maintenance window for dedicated pool patching. Offered assistance for private on-prem patch application.
next_steps: Finish code review and merge hotfix PRs; coordinate with SRE for canary deployment.
Run reconciliation job and validate slab accounting corrections across affected clusters.
Add long-running session tests to nightly mem-stress pipeline and improve alerts around checksum_mismatch_rate.
Follow up with customers to verify stability and close escalation after 72h of no OOMs.
Draft postmortem and update runtime docs with guidance for operators on eviction tuning and known mitigations.
